change.title: pr-3-flat
change.description: feat(upsampling) - Support upsampled error count with performance optimizations
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: transformAliasToInputFormat=1 turns upsampled counts into silent zeros
findings.body: When upsampling applies, `count()` is replaced by `upsampled_count() as count` (organization_events_stats.py:296, also 233 and 277). The result row therefore carries the key `count`. But when the request sets `transformAliasToInputFormat=1` (read at lines 205-207), `resolve_axis_column` returns the input string unchanged (src/sentry/api/bases/organization_events.py:75-76), so the serializer looks up `count()`. `SnubaTSResultSerializer.serialize` does `r.get(column, 0)` (src/sentry/api/serializers/snuba.py:92), so every point comes back 0 with no error. The flag is reachable from the frontend: static/app/views/insights/common/queries/useDiscoverSeries.ts:164 sends it as '1' when a caller sets the option. Fix: when the input-format flag is set, keep the requested key in the transformed column (for example `upsampled_count() as "count()"`), or make the serializer read the same key the query returns. Add a test that sends transformAliasToInputFormat=1 with an allowlisted project.

findings.title: Substring match on 'event.type:error' also matches negated and OR queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` tests `"event.type:error" in query`. That is a substring test, so `!event.type:error` matches, and so does `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. For the discover dataset, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` (lines 122-124) then returns True, and `count()` becomes `upsampled_count()` (sum of sample_weight). The module's own docstring says sample_weight does not exist for transactions (lines 105-107). A query that selects transactions therefore sums a column they lack, which gives zero or an error, and nothing tells the user. The test at tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py:77-88 has no negated or OR case, so it does not catch this. Fix: match the event.type term as a token that is not negated and not part of an OR, and add `!event.type:error` to the test.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses the request dataset, not the dataset each sub-query runs on
findings.body: The eligibility check passes `dataset` (the request-level variable from line 170) at line 220, not `scoped_dataset`. In the dashboard split path (lines 344-380), the request dataset is always a metrics dataset, because the split only runs when `metrics_enhanced` is true (line 344). `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False for metrics datasets (error_upsampling.py:126-127). So split error queries that run on discover with `(query) AND !event.type:transaction` are never upsampled, even for allowlisted projects. The decision also reads the raw request `query` (error_upsampling.py:135), not the rewritten query each split runs. Result: error widgets show raw counts in the split path and upsampled counts elsewhere. Fix: decide per call from the dataset and query the sub-query actually runs. I did not run the dashboard path to confirm the output, so this rests on the code paths read.

findings.title: Upsampling ships behind an option allowlist, not a feature flag
findings.body: CLAUDE.md asks for a feature flag on new features and for experimental features ("Feature Flags: Always add for new features"; "Add feature flags for experimental features"). This change gates the query behaviour on the existing option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` (src/sentry/options/defaults.py:3464) and adds no flag in src/sentry/features. Option allowlists do give a rollout control, but they are not the repository's flag mechanism. Either add a flag to gate the transform, or say in the PR why an option is the intended gate.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache has no callers, and the docstrings contradict the cache
findings.body: The repository search finds no caller for `invalidate_upsampling_cache`; its only occurrence is its definition. Without it, an allowlist change takes up to 60 seconds to reach queries, because the eligibility result is cached (lines 30-38). The docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` (lines 50-53) says the allowlist is read fresh on every call and that this is intentional, which the cache in front of it contradicts. Fix: either call the invalidation from the option-change path, or delete the function and correct the docstring.

findings.title: upsampled_count is public, unlike the other internal helpers in this table
findings.body: The new SnQL function is registered without `private=True`, so users can call `upsampled_count()` directly in queries. Its SQL assumes `sample_weight`, which the module's own docstring says is absent for transactions. The neighbouring internal helpers (`column_hash`, `rounded_timestamp`, `examples`) are marked `private=True`. Mark this one private unless a public function is intended, and say so in the PR.

findings.title: Is sample_weight a real column on the discover and errors entities in Snuba?
findings.body: Nothing in this repository defines a `sample_weight` column. The only references are the new code in this change (`grep` over src/ finds it only at discover.py:1044-1048 and in the helper docstrings). The aggregation `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` is only correct if Snuba's errors and discover storage provides that column with per-event weights. If the column is missing, every upsampled query on an allowlisted project fails. Please confirm against the Snuba schema, and confirm how the weight is computed for a client_sample_rate of 0.1, because the snuba test expects a count of 10 for each event.

findings.title: Test factory sets sample_rate in a way production ingest does not, so the snuba test does not exercise the real pipeline
findings.body: Production only copies `client_sample_rate` into `sample_rate` for allowlisted projects, and only when 0 < rate <= 1 (src/sentry/event_manager.py:776-787). The factory copies it for every event that has the context and does not check the range (factories.py:344-357, called at 1049). The snuba test patches only `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options` (tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py:3604-3607), not the event_manager check. So the expected count of 10 relies on the factory copying a field that real ingest would not set in that setup. The factory also swallows every exception with bare `except Exception: pass` (factories.py:351, 356). Mirror the production gate in the factory, or seed `sample_rate` explicitly in the test and document that.

findings.title: Test creates Organization directly instead of using a create_* helper
findings.body: CLAUDE.md says tests should use `self.create_*` helpers, not direct model creation ("Tests: Use self.create_* helpers, not direct model creation"). Line 21 calls `Organization.objects.create(name="test-org")`. Use `self.create_organization(name="test-org")`.

findings.title: Unrelated change to a public error message
findings.body: The `topEvents` error text changes from "If topEvents needs to be at least 1" to "topEvents needs to be at least 1". This has nothing to do with upsampling, and clients that match the string will break. No test in the repository asserts either form. Move it to its own change, or revert it.

findings.title: Comments describe an optimisation that does not exist; the check runs on every events-stats request
findings.body: The comments at lines 218-226 say the early check is a "performance optimization" and that the stored decision allows "better query optimization and caching". The code does neither: `upsampling_enabled` is a copy of the result. The check runs for every call of `_get_event_stats`, including requests with no `count()` column and RPC datasets that never upsample, so it adds a cache round trip to each events-stats request. Remove the claims, or move the check so it only runs when a `count()` column is present.

findings.title: setUp replaces self.user after login_as, so the logged-in user and self.user differ
findings.body: Line 3559 logs in `self.user`, and line 3560 saves it as `self.authed_user`. Line 3566 then overwrites `self.user` with a new user, which the stored events use as `sentry:user` (lines 3578, 3591). The requests still run as the original user, and `self.authed_user` is never used. This works, but it is confusing. Use a distinct name for the second user, and remove `authed_user` or use it.

summary: Reviewed the eight files of this part. Four findings are "fix" level. The most concrete is that `transformAliasToInputFormat=1` with upsampling returns zeros silently, because the query returns the key `count` while the serializer reads `count()`. The substring check `"event.type:error" in query` also matches negated and OR queries, which pushes transaction rows through `sum(sample_weight)`. The upsampling decision uses the request dataset rather than the dataset each sub-query runs on, so dashboard split queries are never upsampled. The `sentry-repo` gitlink is an unrelated submodule pointer. Other findings: `upsampled_count` is exposed publicly, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no caller and the docstrings contradict the cache, the factory bypasses the production sample-rate gate, and there is an unrelated error-message change. One question remains open: nothing in this repository defines `sample_weight`, so its existence in Snuba is unverified. I read the new code paths in full, but I read only the relevant regions of factories.py, discover.py and the snuba test file, not each file end to end. I did not build or run anything.
